content.text: Build a URL shortener service. Users submit a long URL and get back a short link; visiting the short link redirects to the original. We want to see how many times each link was clicked. It should be safe to expose on the internet and easy to run locally.

content.problemStatement: Build a minimal, internet-safe URL shortener as a Spring Boot 3 / Java 21 HTTP service: create a short code for an absolute http(s) URL, redirect visitors of the short code to the original URL while counting the click, expose per-link click statistics, and provide a health endpoint. v0 runs locally with no external dependencies; persistence is in-memory behind a storage port so a JDBC store can be added without touching the HTTP layer.

functionalRequirements.text: POST /api/links with {url} returns 201 with a 7-character base62 code and the full short URL.
GET /:code redirects (302) to the original URL and records a click.
GET /api/links/:code/stats returns the click count and last click time.
Only absolute http/https URLs are accepted; anything else is a 400.
Unknown codes return 404 on redirect and stats.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Codes are random (not sequential) so links cannot be enumerated.
Redirects use 302 with Cache-Control: no-store so every click is counted.
Runs with `mvn spring-boot:run`; no database or container required for v0.
Storage is behind an interface with a contract test so a durable adapter can be added later.

acceptanceCriteria.then: 201 with a 7-char base62 code and shortUrl = baseUrl/code

acceptanceCriteria.given: javascript:, ftp:, malformed or empty URL

acceptanceCriteria.then: 200 with clicks=2 and a lastClickAt timestamp

assumptions: No authentication in v0; anyone can create links (rate limiting is a v1 concern and is noted as a risk).
'How many times clicked' means a total count plus last click time; referrer/UA breakdowns are v1.
'Safe to expose' means: scheme allowlist on targets, random codes, no caching of redirects, schema-validated input.
In-memory persistence is acceptable for v0 as long as the storage port makes replacement straightforward.

ambiguities.question: What does 'how many times each link was clicked' need to include?

options.description: Total clicks and last click time
options.impact: Trivial in-memory counter; enough for v0.
Requires an event log and aggregation; better as v1 once storage is durable.

ambiguities.resolution: count+last for v0; breakdowns tracked as a follow-up.

ambiguities.question: Does 'safe to expose on the internet' require rate limiting in v0?

options.description: Input validation and random codes only
options.impact: Ships faster; abuse control added with durable storage.

options.description: Per-IP rate limiting on the create endpoint
options.impact: One more dependency and config surface.

ambiguities.resolution: Not in v0; recorded as a risk with a mitigation plan.

risks.mitigation: Scheme allowlist now; denylist/reputation checks and rate limiting in v1.

risks.risk: In-memory store loses data on restart.
risks.mitigation: Documented v0 limitation; storage port + contract test make SQLite/Postgres a contained change.

risks.risk: Code collisions as the keyspace fills.
risks.mitigation: 62^7 keys, collision check with bounded retry.

content.summary: Small hexagonal service: an HTTP adapter (Spring MVC @RestController) over a storage port (LinkStore) with an in-memory adapter, and a pure code-generation class. The controller owns validation and status codes; the store owns links and click counters; Codes owns randomness. Tests boot the real context on a random port and use java.net.http.

components.name: LinkController
components.responsibility: Routes, URL policy, 302/no-store redirects, JSON responses.

components.name: LinkStore port + InMemory adapter
components.responsibility: Persist links and click counters; the seam for a JDBC adapter.

components.name: Codes
components.responsibility: Random base62 codes with rejection sampling; bounded collision retry.

dataFlow: POST /api/links -> validateUrl (http/https only) -> Codes.unique(store::exists) -> store.insert -> 201 {code, shortUrl, targetUrl, createdAt}

decisions.decision: Random base62 codes (7 chars) instead of an encoded counter.
decisions.rationale: Counters are enumerable; random codes with a collision check are not. 62^7 ≈ 3.5e12 keys.
decisions.tradeoffs: Needs an existence check per create; negligible at v0 scale.

decisions.rationale: 301 is cached by browsers, which would hide repeat clicks from analytics.
decisions.tradeoffs: Slightly more traffic to the service; acceptable, analytics is a requirement.

decisions.decision: Storage behind a LinkStore port with an in-memory adapter.
decisions.rationale: Zero-setup local run now; JDBC/Postgres later without touching the controller.
decisions.tradeoffs: Data lost on restart in v0 (documented).

decisions.decision: Validate URLs explicitly in the controller with a scheme allowlist.
decisions.rationale: javascript:/data: targets would make the redirect an XSS vector.

securityConsiderations: Path templates constrain codes to 7 base62 characters
No user input is reflected in responses unescaped
content.rollbackStrategy: v0 is a new service: rollback is stopping the process. No data migration exists.

files.content:
# URL shortener (v0)

Create short links, redirect with click counting, read stats. Spring Boot 3 / Java 21.

```bash
mvn test
mvn spring-boot:run          # http://localhost:8080 ; APP_BASE_URL to change the short-link host
```

## API
| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST | /api/links `{url}` | Create a short link (201) |
| GET | /{code} | 302 redirect, counts the click |
| GET | /api/links/{code}/stats | `{code, clicks, lastClickAt}` |
| GET | /health | Liveness |

Only absolute `http`/`https` URLs are accepted.

## v0 limitations
- In-memory storage: links are lost on restart. `LinkStore` is the seam for a JDBC adapter.
- No rate limiting or authentication. Do not expose publicly without them.
- Stats are a count + last click time; breakdowns come with durable storage.

# ADR-0001: Random base62 codes and 302 redirects

**Status:** accepted

## Decisions
- Short codes are 7 random base62 characters (rejection-sampled) with a bounded collision retry, not an encoded counter: sequential codes let anyone enumerate every link.
- Redirects are `302` with `Cache-Control: no-store`: a `301` would be cached by browsers and hide repeat clicks from analytics.

## Consequences
- One existence check per create; negligible at this scale.
- Slightly more redirect traffic reaches the service; required for click counting.
